title.zh: 卷八十六 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔
title.en: Volume 86 Biographies 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian
title.raw: 卷八十六 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔 Volume 86 Biographies 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十六 殷孝祖 劉勔

translations.literal: Biographies 46: Yin Xiaozu, Liu Mian
translations.idiomatic: Biography 46: Yin Xiaozu and Liu Mian

sentences.zh: 殷孝祖，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Xiaozu was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu came from Changping in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖羨，晉光祿勳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xian was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yin Xian had served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父祖並不達。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather both did not attain distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Neither his father nor his grandfather had risen to prominence.

sentences.zh: 孝祖少誕節，好酒色，有氣幹。

translations.literal: Xiaozu in youth was unconventional in conduct, fond of wine and women, and possessed martial spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xiaozu was unconventional, fond of wine and women, and possessed real martial spirit.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉末，為奉朝請，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era under Emperor Wen, he served as Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen, he held the posts of court gentleman for the imperial audience and supernumerary gentleman attendant at the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其有武用，除奮武將軍、濟北太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, because of his military usefulness, appointed him General Who Exerts Martial Power and Administrator of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, valuing his military ability, appointed him General Who Exerts Martial Power and administrator of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 入為積射將軍。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as General of Accumulated Archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as General of Accumulated Archery.

sentences.zh: 大明初，索虜寇青州，上遣孝祖北援，受刺史顏師伯節度，累與虜戰，頻大破之，事在師伯傳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daming, the Northern Wei raided Qingzhou; the emperor sent Xiaozu north in relief; he came under the command of Inspector Yan Shibo, repeatedly fought the barbarians, and frequently inflicted great defeats—the matter is in Shibo's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daming era, when the Northern Wei raided Qingzhou, the court sent Xiaozu north in relief under Inspector Yan Shibo's command. He fought the enemy again and again and won repeated crushing victories; the account is given in Yan Shibo's biography.

sentences.zh: 還授太子旅賁中郎將，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Central Commandant of the Crown Prince's Rapid-as-Tigers Guard, with the additional title General of the Dragon Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made central commandant of the crown prince's Rapid-as-Tigers guard and given the additional rank of General of the Dragon Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵為逆，孝祖隸沈慶之攻誕，又有戰功，遷西陽王子尚撫軍、寧朔將軍、南濟陰太守。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling Liu Dan held Guangling in rebellion, Xiaozu served under Shen Qingzhi in the attack on Dan, again won battle merit, and was transferred to Staff Officer of the Army for Prince Zishang of Xiyang, General Who Pacifies the North, and Administrator of Southern Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingling, Liu Dan, seized Guangling in revolt, Xiaozu served under Shen Qingzhi against him and again distinguished himself in battle. He was then transferred to staff officer of the army for Prince Zishang of Xiyang, with the ranks of General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Southern Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 出為盱眙太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xuyi, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administrator of Xuyi, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 還為虎賁中郎將，仍除寧朔將軍、陽平、東平二郡太守。

translations.literal: On return he became Tiger Guard Commandant, and was also appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of the two commanderies Yangping and Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became tiger guard commandant and was also appointed General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Yangping and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 又遷濟南、南郡，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was further transferred to Jinan and Nanjun, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Jinan and Nanjun, still holding his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，以本號督兗州諸軍事、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe under the Former Deposed Emperor, with his existing title he supervised military affairs of Yanzhou and became Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jinghe under the Former Deposed Emperor, he was made supervisor of military affairs in Yanzhou and inspector of Yanzhou, retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗初即位，四方反叛，孝祖外甥司徒參軍潁川葛僧韶建議銜命徵孝祖入朝，上遣之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming first took the throne, rebellion broke out on all sides; Xiaozu's nephew, Staff Officer of the Secretariat Ge Sengshao of Yingchuan, proposed that an imperial order summon Xiaozu to court, and the emperor sent him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming first ascended the throne, revolts flared on every side. Xiaozu's nephew Ge Sengshao of Yingchuan, a staff officer of the secretariat, urged that an imperial summons bring Xiaozu to court, and the emperor dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 時徐州刺史薛安都遣薛索兒等屯據津徑，僧韶間行得至，說孝祖曰：「景和兇狂，開闢未有，朝野危極，假命漏刻。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu had sent Xue Suo'er and others to hold the ferry routes; Sengshao by secret paths reached him and urged Xiaozu, saying: "Jinghe was ferocious and mad, unprecedented since the world's beginning; court and countryside were in extreme peril, clinging to life by the drip of the clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andu, inspector of Xuzhou, had sent Xue Suo'er and others to hold the ferry crossings. Sengshao slipped through by hidden routes and urged Xiaozu: "The Jinghe reign was savage and lawless beyond anything since the world's beginning. Court and countryside hung by a thread, life measured out in clepsydra drips.

sentences.zh: 主上聖德天挺，神武在躬，曾不浹辰，夷凶翦暴，更造天地，未足為言。

translations.literal: Our lord's sagely virtue was heaven-endowed, divine martial prowess in his person; in less than ten days he had leveled the vicious and cut down the violent, remaking heaven and earth—words scarcely suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign's sagely virtue is heaven-born, his divine martial prowess in his own person. In less than ten days he has crushed the wicked and cut down the violent, remaking the realm—words can scarcely do it justice.

sentences.zh: 國亂朝危，宜立長生，公卿百辟，人無異議，泰平之隆，非旦則夕。

translations.literal: The state was in turmoil and the court in peril; a mature ruler ought to be established; among the hundred officials none dissented; the grandeur of great peace would come not in the morning then in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: With the state in turmoil and the court in peril, the time called for a mature ruler. Among the hundred officials of state there was no dissent. An age of great peace would come not tomorrow but today.

sentences.zh: 而群小相煽，構造無端，貪利幼弱，競懷希望。

translations.literal: Yet petty men incited one another, fabricating groundless charges, greedy for profit from a youthful and weak ruler, each nursing hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty men stirred one another up, fabricating groundless plots, greedy for advantage from a young and weak sovereign, each nursing his own hopes.

sentences.zh: 使天道助逆，群凶事申，則主幼時艱，權柄不一，兵難互起，豈有自容之地。

translations.literal: If heaven's way aided the rebels and the wicked succeeded, then with a young lord and hard times, power would not be unified, military troubles would rise one after another—where would there be room for oneself?
translations.idiomatic: If heaven favored the rebels and the wicked prevailed, the sovereign would be young, the times harsh, and power divided. War would break out on every side—where would any of us find safety?

sentences.zh: 舅少有立功之志，長以氣節成名，若便能控濟、河義勇，還奉朝廷，非唯匡主靜亂，乃可以垂名竹帛。

translations.literal: Uncle, you from youth had the will to achieve merit; grown up you were famed for spirit and integrity—if you could now command the righteous volunteers of Ji and the Yellow River and return to serve the court, you would not only aid the lord and still the turmoil but could leave your name on silk and bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, you have wanted glory since youth and are famed for spirit and integrity. If you can rally the loyal volunteers of Ji and the Yellow River and return to serve the court, you will not only restore the sovereign and quell the chaos—you will win a name that lives in the histories.

sentences.zh: 」孝祖具問朝廷消息，僧韶隨方酬譬，並陳兵甲精強，主上欲委以前驅之任。

translations.literal: " Xiaozu questioned him fully on court news; Sengshao answered as occasion required, and also declared the troops and armor excellent, that the sovereign wished to entrust him with the vanguard command.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaozu questioned him closely about affairs at court. Sengshao answered to each point and reported that the army was strong and well equipped, and that the sovereign wished to entrust him with the vanguard command.

sentences.zh: 孝祖即日棄妻子，率文武二千人隨僧韶還都。

translations.literal: That very day Xiaozu abandoned wife and children, led two thousand civil and military followers with Sengshao back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Xiaozu left wife and children behind and led two thousand civil and military followers back to the capital with Sengshao.

sentences.zh: 時普天同逆，朝廷唯保丹陽一郡，而永世縣尋又反叛。

translations.literal: At the time all under heaven rebelled together; the court held only Danyang commandery, and soon Yongshi county rebelled as well.
translations.idiomatic: All the empire had risen in revolt; the court held only Danyang commandery, and before long Yongshi county rebelled too.

sentences.zh: 義興賊垂至延陵，內外憂危，咸欲奔散。

translations.literal: Rebels from Yixing were about to reach Yanling; inside and outside were anxious and perilous; all wished to flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Yixing were nearly at Yanling. Inside and outside the court were in dread, and everyone wanted to flee.

sentences.zh: 孝祖忽至，眾力不少，並傖楚壯士，人情於是大安。

translations.literal: Xiaozu suddenly arrived; his force was not small, all northern and Chu stalwarts; popular feeling then greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozu arrived unexpectedly, his force was substantial—all northern and Chu veterans—and morale at once steadied.

sentences.zh: 進孝祖號冠軍，假節、督前鋒諸軍事，遣向虎檻，拒對南賊。

translations.literal: Xiaozu was advanced in title to General Who Conquers the Champions, given temporary credentials and command of vanguard military affairs, and sent toward Tiger Cage to oppose the southern rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu was promoted to General Who Conquers the Champions, given temporary credentials as supervisor of vanguard forces, and sent to Tiger Cage to face the southern rebels.

sentences.zh: 御仗先有諸葛亮筒袖鎧帽，二十五石弩射之不能入，上悉以賜孝祖。

translations.literal: Among the imperial armory were tube-sleeve armor and caps of the Zhuge Liang type; a twenty-five-stone crossbow could not pierce them—the emperor bestowed them all on Xiaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armory held tube-sleeve armor and caps of the Zhuge Liang pattern, proof even against a twenty-five-stone crossbow. The emperor gave them all to Xiaozu.

sentences.zh: 孝祖負其誠節，凌轢諸將，臺軍有父子兄弟在南者，孝祖並欲推治。

translations.literal: Xiaozu, relying on his loyal integrity, rode roughshod over the generals; among the capital troops, those who had fathers, sons, or brothers in the south—Xiaozu wished to investigate and punish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his own loyalty, Xiaozu bullied the other generals. Where capital troops had fathers, sons, or brothers serving with the rebels in the south, he wanted them all investigated and punished.

sentences.zh: 由是人情乖離，莫樂為用。

translations.literal: Hence popular feeling turned away; none were willing to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Men's hearts turned from him, and none were willing to fight wholeheartedly under his command.

sentences.zh: 進使持節、都督兗州、青、冀、幽四州諸軍事、撫軍將軍，刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs of the four provinces Yan, Qing, Ji, and You, General Who Pacifies the Army, inspector unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to bearer of the staff of authority, supervisor of military affairs in Yan, Qing, Ji, and You, and General Who Pacifies the Army, while retaining his inspectorship.

sentences.zh: 時賊據赭圻，孝祖將進攻之，與大統王玄謨別，悲不自勝，眾並駭怪。

translations.literal: At the time the rebels held Zheqi; Xiaozu was about to attack; taking leave of Grand Commander Wang Xuanmo, he was overcome with grief beyond control—all were startled and wondered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Zheqi, and Xiaozu was about to attack. When he took leave of Grand Commander Wang Xuanmo, he was overcome with grief. All who saw it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年三月三日，與賊合戰，常以鼓蓋自隨，軍中人相謂曰：「殷統軍可謂死矣。

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month of the second year of Taishi, he joined battle with the rebels, always keeping drum and canopy with him; men in the army said to one another: "Commander Yin is as good as dead.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the third month of the second year of Taishi he met the rebels in battle, always keeping his drum and battle canopy with him. Men in the ranks said to one another, "Commander Yin might as well be dead already.

sentences.zh: 今與賊交鋒，而以羽儀自標顯，若善射者十士攢射，欲不斃，得乎？

translations.literal: Now he crosses blades with the enemy yet displays his regalia to mark himself—if ten skilled archers shoot together, how can he not be killed?"
translations.idiomatic: He is in the thick of the fight yet flaunts his ceremonial regalia. If ten good archers shoot at once, how can he fail to fall?"

sentences.zh: 」是日，於陣為矢所中死，時年五十二。

translations.literal: " That day, in the battle line he was struck by an arrow and died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: " That day he was struck by an arrow in the battle line and died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、征北將軍，持節、都督如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Palace Secretariat and General Who Campaigns North, bearer of the staff and supervisor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as attendant-in-ordinary at the palace secretariat and General Who Campaigns North, retaining his credentials as bearer of the staff and his supervisory command.

sentences.zh: 封秭歸縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zigui county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zigui with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 四年，追改封建安縣，諡曰忠侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his fief was changed posthumously to Jian'an county; his posthumous title was Loyal Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his fief was changed posthumously to Jian'an county, with the posthumous title Loyal Marquis.

sentences.zh: 孝祖子悉為薛安都所殺，以從兄子慧達繼封。

translations.literal: All Xiaozu's sons were killed by Xue Andu; his cousin's son Huida succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: All of Xiaozu's sons were killed by Xue Andu, and his cousin's son Huida inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 劉勔，字伯猷，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Mian, styled Boyou, was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian, courtesy name Boyou, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖懷義，始興太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huaiyi was Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Huaiyi had been administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 父穎之，汝南、新蔡二郡太守，征林邑，遇疾卒。

translations.literal: His father Yingzhi was Administrator of the two commanderies Runan and Xincai; campaigning against Linyi, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Yingzhi had been administrator of Runan and Xincai. On campaign against Linyi he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 勔少有志節，兼好文義。

translations.literal: Mian from youth had resolve and integrity, and also loved literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Mian showed resolve and integrity and also loved literary learning.

sentences.zh: 家貧，為廣州增城令，廣州刺史劉道錫引為揚烈府主簿。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he served as Magistrate of Zengcheng in Guangzhou; Inspector of Guangzhou Liu Daoxi brought him in as Chief Clerk of the Yanglie headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor. He served as magistrate of Zengcheng in Guangzhou until Inspector Liu Daoxi took him on as chief clerk of the Yanglie headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，索虜南侵，道錫遣勔奉使詣京都，太祖引見之，酬對稱旨，除寧遠將軍、綏遠太守。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Northern Wei invaded south; Daoxi sent Mian on embassy to the capital; Emperor Wen received him in audience; his replies pleased the emperor; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Administrator of Suiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, when the Northern Wei invaded the south, Daoxi sent Mian to the capital on embassy. Emperor Wen received him in audience and was pleased with his replies. He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and administrator of Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，蕭簡據廣州為亂，勔起義討之，燒其南門。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia Xiao Jian held Guangzhou in rebellion; Mian raised righteous troops to attack him and burned the southern gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia, Xiao Jian seized Guangzhou in revolt. Mian raised loyal troops against him and burned the southern gate.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史宗愨又命為軍府主簿，以功封大亭侯。

translations.literal: Inspector of Guangzhou Zong Que again appointed him Chief Clerk of the army headquarters; for merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dating.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zong Que of Guangzhou again made him chief clerk of the army headquarters, and for his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dating.

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supernumerary gentleman attendant at the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，荊、江反叛，宗愨以勔行寧朔將軍、湘東內史，領軍出安陸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian Jing and Jiang rebelled; Zong Que had Mian act as General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Minister of Xiangdong, leading troops out from Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojian era, when Jing and Jiang rebelled, Zong Que had Mian serve as General Who Pacifies the North and interior minister of Xiangdong, leading troops out from Anlu.

sentences.zh: 會事平，以本號為晉康太守，又徙鬱林太守。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, with his existing title he became Administrator of Jinkang, then was transferred to Administrator of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt was settled, he was made administrator of Jinkang under his existing rank, then transferred to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 大明初還都，徐州刺史劉道隆請為寧朔司馬。

translations.literal: Early in Daming he returned to the capital; Inspector of Xuzhou Liu Daolong requested him as Chief of Staff for the Pacification of the North.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daming era he returned to the capital, and Inspector Liu Daolong of Xuzhou asked to have him as his chief of staff for the Pacification of the North.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵為逆，勔隨道隆受沈慶之節度，事平，封金城縣五等侯。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingling Liu Dan held Guangling in rebellion, Mian followed Daolong under Shen Qingzhi's command; when affairs were settled he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Jincheng county.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingling, Liu Dan, seized Guangling in revolt, Mian followed Daolong under Shen Qingzhi's command. When the revolt was crushed he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 除西陽王子尚撫軍參軍，入直閣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Army Staff Officer to the Pacification Army for Prince Zishang of Xiyang, and entered duty in the Inner Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made army staff officer to Prince Zishang of Xiyang's pacification army and entered duty in the inner pavilion.

sentences.zh: 先是，遣費沈伐陳檀，不克，乃除勔龍驤將軍、西江督護、鬱林太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fei Shen had been sent to attack Chen Tan and failed; then Mian was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry, Protector of the Western River, and Administrator of Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fei Shen had been sent against Chen Tan without success. Mian was then appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry, protector of the Western River, and administrator of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 勔既至，率軍進討，隨宜翦定，大致名馬，并獻珊瑚連理樹，上甚悅。

translations.literal: When Mian arrived, he led troops forward in attack, pacifying as circumstances required, obtaining many famous horses, and also presenting a coral tree with conjoined trunks—the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mian arrived, he led his troops forward, pacifying the region as circumstances required. He obtained many fine horses and also presented a coral tree with conjoined trunks. The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 還除新安王子鸞撫軍中兵參軍，遭母憂，不拜。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Central Army Staff Officer to the Pacification Army for Prince Ziluan of Xin'an; he encountered mourning for his mother and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed central army staff officer to Prince Ziluan of Xin'an's pacification army, but when his mother died he declined the post.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，起為振威將軍、屯騎校尉，入直閣。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was recalled as General Who Shakes Might and Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, entering duty in the Inner Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, Mian was recalled to serve as General Who Shakes Might and colonel of the garrison cavalry, again on duty in the inner pavilion.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，加寧朔將軍，校尉如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North, colonel unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he was given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the North while retaining his colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史晉安王子勛為逆，四方回應，勔以本官領建平王景素輔國司馬，進據梁山。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Prince Zixun of Jin'an rebelled; the four quarters responded; Mian with his existing office also served as Chief of Staff to the State-Assisting Army for Prince Jingsu of Jianping, advancing to hold Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zixun of Jin'an, inspector of Jiangzhou, rebelled and the empire answered him, Mian retained his existing post while also serving as chief of staff to the state-assisting army of Prince Jingsu of Jianping, advancing to hold Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 會豫州刺史殷琰反叛，徵勔還都，假輔國將軍，率眾討琰，甲仗三十人入六門。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Yuzhou Yin Yan rebelled, Mian was summoned back to the capital, given temporary rank as General Who Assists the State, led troops to attack Yan, and thirty men with arms and armor entered the Six Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Yan, inspector of Yuzhou, rebelled, Mian was recalled to the capital, given temporary rank as General Who Assists the State, and sent to attack him with thirty armed men admitted through the Six Gates.

sentences.zh: 復兼山陽王休祐驃騎司馬，餘如故。

translations.literal: He also concurrently served as Chief of Staff to the Rapid Cavalry for Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as chief of staff to the rapid cavalry of Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang, his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 破琰將劉順於宛唐，杜叔寶於橫塘，事在琰傳。

translations.literal: He defeated Yan's generals Liu Shun at Wantang and Du Shubao at Hengtang—the matter is in Yan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Yan's generals Liu Shun at Wantang and Du Shubao at Hengtang; the account is given in Yin Yan's biography.

sentences.zh: 除輔國將軍、山陽王休祐驃騎諮議參軍、梁郡太守、假節，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Assists the State, Staff Adviser to the Rapid Cavalry for Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang, Administrator of Liang commandery, and given temporary credentials—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the posts of General Who Assists the State, staff adviser to Prince Xiuyou's rapid cavalry, and administrator of Liang, with temporary credentials—but he declined.

sentences.zh: 琰嬰城固守，自始春至於末冬，薛道標、龐孟虯並向壽陽，勔內攻外禦，戰無不捷。

translations.literal: Yan held the city fast from early spring to late winter; Xue Daobiao and Pang Mengjiao both marched on Shouyang; Mian attacked within and defended without—every battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Yan held the city from early spring to late winter. Xue Daobiao and Pang Mengjiao both marched on Shouyang. Mian attacked within and defended without, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 善撫將帥，以寬厚為眾所依。

translations.literal: He was skilled in comforting generals and officers, and with generosity and breadth was relied on by all.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at winning over his officers and relied on generosity and breadth of spirit to hold their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 將軍王廣之求勔所自乘馬，諸將帥並忿廣之叨冒，勸勔以法裁之，勔歡笑，即時解馬與廣之。

translations.literal: General Wang Guangzhi asked for the horse Mian himself rode; the generals and officers all resented Guangzhi's presumption and urged Mian to punish him by law; Mian laughed and at once gave him the horse.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Guangzhi asked for Mian's own mount. The other commanders resented his presumption and urged Mian to punish him. Mian only laughed and at once gave him the horse.

sentences.zh: 復除使持節、督廣、交二州諸軍事、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，將軍如故，不拜。

translations.literal: He was again appointed bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs of the two provinces Guang and Jiao, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou, general's title unchanged—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was again offered the posts of bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Guang and Jiao, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou, while retaining his general's rank—but again he declined.

sentences.zh: 及琰開門請降，勔約令三軍，不得妄動。

translations.literal: When Yan opened the gates to surrender, Mian bound the three armies by order not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan opened the gates to surrender, Mian bound the three armies by strict order not to act rashly.

sentences.zh: 城內士民，秋毫無所失，百姓感悅，咸曰來蘇。

translations.literal: Within the city, civilians lost not a hair's breadth; the people were moved and pleased, all saying they had been restored to life.
translations.idiomatic: The people in the city lost not a hair's breadth of their property. Grateful and rejoicing, they said the savior had come again.

sentences.zh: 百姓生為立碑。

translations.literal: While he lived the people erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: In his lifetime the people erected a monument to him.

sentences.zh: 改督益、寧二州諸軍事、益州刺史，持節、將軍如故，又不拜。

translations.literal: His supervision was changed to military affairs of the two provinces Yi and Ning and Inspector of Yi, bearer of the staff and general unchanged—again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered supervision of military affairs in Yi and Ning and the inspectorship of Yi, retaining his credentials and general's rank—but again he declined.

sentences.zh: 還京都，拜太子左衛率，封鄱陽縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was appointed Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he was appointed left commandant of the crown prince's guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Poyang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 琰初求救索虜，虜大眾屯據汝南。

translations.literal: Yan at first sought aid from the Northern Wei; the barbarians' great host encamped and held Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had first sought aid from the Northern Wei, and a great barbarian host now held Runan.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，以勔為征虜將軍、督西討前鋒諸軍事，假節、置佐、本官如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi, Mian was made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and supervisor of vanguard military affairs of the western punitive expedition, with temporary credentials, staff appointed, and his original offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taishi, Mian was appointed General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and supervisor of the western punitive vanguard, with temporary credentials and a full staff, while retaining his existing posts.

sentences.zh: 先是，常珍奇據汝南，與琰為逆，琰降，因據戍降虜，事在琰傳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chang Zhenqi held Runan and rebelled with Yan; when Yan surrendered, he held the garrison and submitted to the barbarians—the matter is in Yan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chang Zhenqi had held Runan and rebelled alongside Yin Yan. When Yan surrendered, Zhenqi held the garrison and went over to the barbarians; the account is in Yin Yan's biography.

sentences.zh: 至是引虜西河公、長社公攻圍輔國將軍、汝陰太守張景遠。

translations.literal: At this time he brought in the barbarian Princes of Xihe and Changshe to attack and besiege General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Ruyin Zhang Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He now brought in the barbarian princes of Xihe and Changshe to attack and besiege General Who Assists the State Zhang Jingyuan, administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 景遠與軍主楊文萇拒擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Jingyuan with Army Commander Yang Wenchang resisted and struck, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan and army commander Yang Wenchang met them in battle and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 景遠尋病卒，太宗嘉其功，追贈冠軍將軍、豫州刺史，追封含洭縣男，食邑三百戶，以文萇代為汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Jingyuan soon died of illness; Emperor Ming praised his merit and posthumously gave him General Who Conquers the Champions and Inspector of Yuzhou, posthumously enfeoffed him as Baron of Hanqiu county with a fief of three hundred households, and had Wenchang replace him as Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan soon died of illness. Emperor Ming praised his achievement and posthumously honored him as General Who Conquers the Champions and inspector of Yuzhou, enfeoffing him as Baron of Hanqiu with three hundred households. Yang Wenchang succeeded him as administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 除勔右衛將軍，仍以為使持節、都督豫、司二州諸軍事、征虜將軍、豫州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: Mian was appointed General of the Right Guard, and still made bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs of the two provinces Yu and Si, General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and Inspector of Yuzhou; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was appointed General of the Right Guard and also made bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yu and Si, General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and inspector of Yuzhou, his other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四年，除侍中，領射聲校尉，又不受。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Palace Attendant and Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound—again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was offered the posts of palace attendant and colonel of the archers who shoot at sound, but again he declined.

sentences.zh: 進號右將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was advanced to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 其年，虜遣汝陽司馬趙懷仁步騎五百，寇武津縣。

translations.literal: That year the barbarians sent Chief of Staff of Ruyang Zhao Huairen with five hundred infantry and cavalry to raid Wujin county.
translations.idiomatic: That year the barbarians sent Zhao Huairen, chief of staff of Ruyang, with five hundred infantry and cavalry to raid Wujin county.

sentences.zh: 勔遣龍驤將軍曲元德輕兵進討，虜眾驚散。

translations.literal: Mian sent General of the Dragon Cavalry Qu Yuande with light troops forward in attack; the barbarian host scattered in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Mian sent General of the Dragon Cavalry Qu Yuande with light troops against them, and the barbarian force scattered in alarm.

sentences.zh: 虜子都公閼於拔又率三百人防運車囗囗千兩，於汝陽臺東水上結營。

translations.literal: The barbarian Prince of the Capital District Yan Yu Ba again led three hundred men to defend transport carts [lacuna in text] one thousand three hundred loads, and encamped east of the water at Ruyang Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian prince of the capital district, Yan Yu Ba, again led three hundred men to guard transport wagons—one thousand three hundred loads, by parallel accounts—and encamped on the east bank at Ruyang Terrace.

sentences.zh: 元德單騎直入，斬拔首，因進攻汝陽臺，即陷外壘，獲車一千三百乘，斬首一百五十級。

translations.literal: Yuande alone on horseback charged straight in, beheaded Ba, then advanced to attack Ruyang Terrace, immediately taking the outer rampart, capturing one thousand three hundred carts, and taking one hundred fifty heads.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande charged in alone on horseback, beheaded Ba, then attacked Ruyang Terrace, took the outer rampart at once, captured thirteen hundred wagons, and took one hundred fifty heads.

sentences.zh: 勔又使司徒參軍孫曇瓘督弋陽以西，會虜寇義陽，曇瓘大破之。

translations.literal: Mian also sent Staff Officer of the Secretariat Sun Tanhuan to command west of Yiyang; when the barbarians raided Yiyang, Tanhuan inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Mian also sent secretariat staff officer Sun Tanhuan to command the region west of Yiyang. When the barbarians raided Yiyang, Tanhuan won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 虜上其北豫州租，有車二千兩，勔招荒人，邀擊於許昌，虜眾奔散，焚燒米穀。

translations.literal: The barbarians were transporting the tax grain of their Northern Yuzhou, with two thousand carts; Mian recruited frontier people and intercepted them at Xuchang; the barbarian host fled and scattered, and the rice grain was burned.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians were moving the tax grain of Northern Yuzhou in two thousand wagons. Mian rallied frontier people and ambushed them at Xuchang. The barbarian force fled in disorder, and the grain was burned.

sentences.zh: 淮西人賈元友上書太宗，勸北攻懸瓠，可收陳郡、南頓、汝南、新蔡四郡之地。

translations.literal: Jia Yuanyou of Huaixi submitted a memorial to Emperor Ming urging a northern attack on Xuanhu, by which the territory of the four commanderies Chen, Nandun, Runan, and Xincai could be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yuanyou of Huaixi memorialized Emperor Ming urging a northern attack on Xuanhu that would recover Chen, Nandun, Runan, and Xincai.

sentences.zh: 上以所陳示勔，使具條答。

translations.literal: The emperor showed what had been stated to Mian and had him answer item by item.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the memorial to Mian and ordered him to reply point by point.

sentences.zh: 勔對曰：

translations.literal: Mian replied:
translations.idiomatic: Mian replied:

sentences.zh: 元友稱：「虜主幼弱，姦偽競起，內外規亂，天亡有期。

translations.literal: Yuanyou stated: "The barbarian lord is young and weak; treachery and falsehood rise in rivalry; inside and outside plot turmoil; heaven's destruction has its term."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou claims: "The barbarian ruler is young and weak, treachery and deceit abound, turmoil is plotted within and without, and heaven's destruction of them is only a matter of time."

sentences.zh: 」臣以為獯醜侵縱，乘藉王境，盤據州郡，百姓殘亡。

translations.literal: " Your servant holds that the Xiongnu barbarians invade wantonly, riding on the royal domain, entrenched in provinces and commanderies, the people slaughtered and perishing.
translations.idiomatic: " I hold that the barbarians invade wantonly, exploiting our royal domain, entrenched in provinces and commanderies, while the people are slaughtered and ruined.

sentences.zh: 去冬眾軍失耕，今春連城圍逼，國家復境之略，實有不遑，滅虜未及。

translations.literal: Last winter the armies lost their planting; this spring linked cities are pressed by siege; the state's strategy of recovering territory truly has no leisure; destroying the barbarians is not yet timely.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter our armies missed the planting season. This spring linked cities are under siege. The state's strategy of recovering lost territory truly allows no leisure for destroying the barbarians—not yet.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「有七千餘家，穀米豐積，可供二萬人數年資儲。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "There are more than seven thousand households, grain and rice abundantly stored, sufficient to supply provisions for twenty thousand men for several years."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "There are more than seven thousand households with grain abundantly stored, enough to supply twenty thousand men for several years."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為二萬人歲食米四十八萬斛，五年合須米二百四十萬斛，既理不容有，恐事難稱言。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that twenty thousand men annually consume four hundred eighty thousand hu of rice; five years together would require two million four hundred thousand hu—since reason cannot allow this, I fear the matter is hard to square with the claim.
translations.idiomatic: " I further calculate that twenty thousand men consume four hundred eighty thousand hu of rice a year; over five years that would be two million four hundred thousand hu. Reason cannot allow such stores, and I fear the claim cannot be squared with fact.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「虜於懸瓠開驛保，虜已先據，若不足恃，此不須囗。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "The barbarians opened relay stations and forts at Xuanhu; the barbarians already hold them first—if they cannot be relied upon, there is no need for concern about this [lacuna in text]."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The barbarians have opened relay stations and forts at Xuanhu and already hold them—if those cannot be relied upon, there is no need to worry about this point [text defective]."

sentences.zh: 」俱是攻城，便應先圖懸瓠，何更越先取郾，以受腹背之災。

translations.literal: " Both are siege warfare—one ought first to target Xuanhu; why instead leap ahead to take Yan first and suffer disaster from front and rear?
translations.idiomatic: " Both operations are sieges, so we ought to take Xuanhu first. Why leap ahead to seize Yan and invite disaster from front and rear?

sentences.zh: 且七千餘家豐積，而虜猶當遠運為糧，是威不制民，民非異計。

translations.literal: Moreover, with more than seven thousand households in abundant stores, yet the barbarians must still transport grain from afar—this shows their authority does not control the people; the people are not of a different mind.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if more than seven thousand households had such abundance, the barbarians would not still be hauling grain from afar. That shows their authority does not control the people, and the people are not truly on their side.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「虜欲水陸運糧，以救軍命，可襲之機，在於今日。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "The barbarians wish to transport grain by land and water to save the army's life; the opportunity for a raid lies in today."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The barbarians plan to move grain by land and water to sustain their army. The moment to strike is now."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為開立驛道，據守堅城，觀其形候，不似蹙弱。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that they have opened relay roads and hold fast to strong cities; observing their bearing and signs, they do not seem pressed and weak.
translations.idiomatic: " I further observe that they have opened relay roads and hold strong cities. Judging by their bearing, they do not look pressed or weak.

sentences.zh: 可乘之機，恐為難驗。

translations.literal: An opportunity to exploit— I fear it will be hard to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Any opportunity to exploit them will be hard to verify in advance.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「四郡民人，遭虜二十七年之毒，皆欲雪仇報恥，伏待朝威。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "The people of the four commanderies, having suffered the barbarians' poison for twenty-seven years, all wish to wash away shame and repay injury, bowing to await the court's majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The people of the four commanderies have suffered under the barbarians for twenty-seven years. They all long to avenge their wrongs and await the court's authority."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為垣式寶等受國重恩，今猶驅略車營，翻還就賊，蓋是戀本之情深，非報怨之宜，何可輕試。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that Yuan Shibao and others received heavy grace from the state, yet still drive and plunder wagon camps and turn back to join the rebels—this is surely deep attachment to their homeland, not the proper mood for repaying grievances; how can one lightly test them?
translations.idiomatic: " I further note that Yuan Shibao and others received great favor from the state, yet still raid wagon camps and return to the enemy. That shows deep attachment to their homeland, not a will to revenge. How can we lightly trust them?

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「請敕荊、雍兩州，遣二千精兵，從義陽依西山北下，直據郾城。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "Please order the two provinces Jing and Yong to send two thousand elite troops from Yiyang along the western hills northward, directly seizing Yancheng."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also asks that Jing and Yong be ordered to send two thousand elite troops from Yiyang along the western hills northward to seize Yancheng directly.

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為郾城是賊驛路要戍，且經蠻接險，數百里中，裹糧潛進，方出平地，攻賊堅城，自古名將，未有能以此濟者。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that Yancheng is a vital garrison on the rebels' relay route, and the route passes through barbarian territory and dangerous ground; for several hundred li, carrying grain and advancing secretly, only then reaching open country to attack the rebels' strong city—from antiquity's famous generals, none has succeeded by this means.
translations.idiomatic: " Yancheng is a vital post on the enemy relay route, and the way passes through barbarian country and rugged terrain. To march several hundred li with bundled grain in secret, then emerge onto open ground and assault a strong enemy city—no famous general of old ever succeeded by such a plan.

sentences.zh: 假其克捷，不知足南抗懸瓠，北捍長社與不？

translations.literal: Supposing they achieved victory, who knows whether they would suffice to resist Xuanhu in the south and hold Changshe in the north or not?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they won, who knows whether they could hold Xuanhu in the south and Changshe in the north?

sentences.zh: 且賊擁據數城，水陸通便，而今使官以二千斷其資運，於事為難。

translations.literal: Moreover the rebels hold several cities with convenient land and water routes; now to send officials with two thousand to cut off their supplies and transport is difficult in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the enemy holds several cities with easy land and water communications. To cut their supply lines with only two thousand men is impracticable.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「虜圍逼汝陰，遊魂二歲，為張景遠所挫，不敢渡淮。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "The barbarians besieged and pressed Ruyin; wandering spirits for two years; they were checked by Zhang Jingyuan and did not dare cross the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The barbarians besieged Ruyin for two years like lost souls until Zhang Jingyuan checked them, and they did not dare cross the Huai."

sentences.zh: 」臣又以為景遠兵力寡弱，不能自固，遠遣救援，方得少克。

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that Jingyuan's troops were few and weak, unable to secure himself; only when relief was sent from afar did he achieve a small victory.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingyuan's force was small and weak and could not hold on its own. Only when distant relief arrived did he win a modest success.

sentences.zh: 今定是為賊所畏不？

translations.literal: Are they now certainly feared by the rebels or not?
translations.idiomatic: Are they now truly feared by the enemy?

sentences.zh: 景遠前所摧傷，裁至數百，虜步騎四萬，猶不敢前，而今必勸國家以輕兵遠討，指掌可克，言理相背，莫復過此。

translations.literal: The damage Jingyuan inflicted before amounted to only several hundred; the barbarians had forty thousand infantry and cavalry yet still did not dare advance—yet now he must urge the state to campaign far with light troops, conquerable at a gesture; reason and claim oppose each other—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan's earlier blows killed only a few hundred. Forty thousand barbarian horse and foot still would not advance—yet now he urges the state to campaign far with light troops and promises victory at a gesture. Nothing could be more contrary to reason.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「龍山雉水，魯奴、王景直等並受朝爵，馬步萬餘。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "At Longshan and Zhishui, Lu Nu, Wang Jingzhi, and others all received court enfeoffments, with more than ten thousand horse and foot."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "At Longshan and Zhishui, Lu Nu, Wang Jingzhi, and others all hold court titles and command more than ten thousand horse and foot."

sentences.zh: 進討之宜，唯須敕命。

translations.literal: The propriety of advancing in attack requires only an imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: They need only an imperial order to advance.

sentences.zh: 」臣以為魯奴與虜交關，彌歷年世，去歲送誠朝廷，誓欲立功。

translations.literal: " Your servant holds that Lu Nu has had dealings with the barbarians spanning many years; last year he sent sincerity to the court, swearing to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu Nu has dealt with the barbarians for many years. Last year he offered loyalty to the court and swore to win merit.

sentences.zh: 自蒙榮爵，便即逃遁，殊類姦猾，豈易闇期。

translations.literal: Once he received honored rank, he at once fled and vanished—utterly unlike treacherous cunning; how easy to reckon on him in secret?
translations.idiomatic: Once he received an honored title he fled at once. Such men are treacherous beyond reckoning. How can we count on them in secret?

sentences.zh: 兼王景直是一亡命，部曲不過數十人，既不可言，又未足恃。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Jingzhi is a mere fugitive; his followers number no more than several tens—he can scarcely be spoken of, and is not sufficient to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingzhi is only a fugitive with a few dozen followers. He is scarcely worth mentioning and cannot be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 萬餘之言，似不近實。

translations.literal: The claim of more than ten thousand seems not close to fact.
translations.idiomatic: The claim of more than ten thousand men seems far from fact.

sentences.zh: 元友又云：「四郡恨忿此非類，車營連結，廢田二載，生業已盡，賊無所資，糧儲已罄。

translations.literal: Yuanyou also said: "The four commanderies hate and resent these alien kinds; wagon camps link together; fields lie waste for two years; livelihoods are exhausted; the rebels have no resources; grain stores are empty."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou also says: "The four commanderies hate these alien invaders. Their wagon camps are linked, fields lie waste for two years, livelihoods are gone, the enemy has no resources, and grain stores are empty."

sentences.zh: 斷其運道，最是要略。

translations.literal: Cutting off their transport routes is the most essential strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting their supply routes is the essential strategy.

sentences.zh: 」臣又以斷運須兵，兵應資食，而當此過懸瓠二百里中，使兵食兼足，何處求辦？

translations.literal: " Your servant further holds that cutting transport requires troops, and troops require provisions—yet in this stretch of two hundred li past Xuanhu, to make both troops and food sufficient, where would one obtain them?
translations.idiomatic: " Cutting supply lines requires troops, and troops require food. In two hundred li of country beyond Xuanhu, where are we to obtain both men and provisions?

sentences.zh: 臣竊尋元嘉以來，傖荒遠人，多干國議，負儋歸闕，皆勸討虜。

translations.literal: Your servant privately reviews that since Yuanjia, northern and frontier people have often interfered in state deliberations; bearing loads they return to the court, all urging campaigns against the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: I have reviewed affairs since the Yuanjia era: frontier and northern peoples have often meddled in state policy, coming to court laden with arguments, all urging campaigns against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 魯爽誕說，實挫國威，徒失兵力，虛費金寶。

translations.literal: The schemes of Lu Shuang and Liu Dan truly damaged national prestige, vainly losing military strength and wasting gold and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The schemes urged by Lu Shuang and Liu Dan truly damaged national prestige, wasting troops and treasure to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 凡此之徒，每規近說，從來信納，皆詒後悔。

translations.literal: All such persons each plot immediate proposals; whenever accepted in the past, they brought later regret.
translations.idiomatic: Such men always urge immediate action. Whenever the court has believed them, it has later regretted it.

sentences.zh: 界上之人，唯視強弱，王師至境，必壺漿候塗，裁見退軍，便抄截蜂起。

translations.literal: People on the borders look only to strength and weakness; when the royal army reaches the frontier they surely bring broth and wait by the road; but at the mere sight of a retreating army, raiding and interception swarm up like bees.
translations.idiomatic: Border people watch only which side is strong. When the imperial army arrives they bring broth to the road, but the moment they see troops withdraw, raiders swarm up like bees.

sentences.zh: 首領回師，何嘗不為河畔所弊。

translations.literal: When commanders lead the army back, when have they not been harried along the riverbanks?
translations.idiomatic: When commanders withdraw, when have they not been harried along the riverbanks?

sentences.zh: 太宗納之，元友議遂寢。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming accepted this; Yuanyou's proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming accepted Mian's view, and Yuanyou's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 勔與常珍奇書，勸令反虜，珍奇乃與子超越、羽林監式寶，於譙殺虜子都公費拔等凡三千餘人。

translations.literal: Mian wrote to Chang Zhenqi urging him to turn against the barbarians; Zhenqi then with his son Chaoyue and Feathered Forest Inspector Shibao at Qiao killed the barbarian Prince of the Capital District Fei Ba and others, more than three thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: Mian wrote to Chang Zhenqi urging him to turn against the barbarians. Zhenqi then joined his son Chaoyue and feathered forest inspector Shibao at Qiao in killing the barbarian prince of the capital district, Fei Ba, and more than three thousand others.

sentences.zh: 勔馳驛以聞，太宗大喜，以珍奇為使持節、都督司、北豫二州諸軍事、平北將軍、司州刺史，汝南、新蔡縣侯，食邑千戶；

translations.literal: Mian sent word by post horse; Emperor Ming was greatly pleased and made Zhenqi bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs of the two provinces Si and Northern Yu, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Sizhou, Marquis of Runan and Xincai counties, fief of one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Mian reported by relay horse. Emperor Ming was overjoyed and made Zhenqi bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Si and Northern Yu, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Sizhou, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Runan and Xincai with a fief of one thousand households;

sentences.zh: 超越輔國將軍、北豫州刺史，潁川、汝陽、囗囗三郡太守，安陽縣男；

translations.literal: Chaoyue as General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Northern Yu, Administrator of the three commanderies Yingchuan, Ruyang, and [lacuna in text], Baron of Anyang county;
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyue as General Who Assists the State and inspector of Northern Yu, administrator of Yingchuan, Ruyang, and two other commanderies named in the text but now lost, and Baron of Anyang;

sentences.zh: 式寶輔國將軍、陳、南頓二郡太守，真陽縣男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Shibao as General Who Assists the State, Administrator of the two commanderies Chen and Nandun, Baron of Zhenyang county, fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shibao as General Who Assists the State and administrator of Chen and Nandun, Baron of Zhenyang with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 珍奇為虜所攻，引軍南出，虜追擊破之，珍奇走依山，得至壽陽，超越、式寶為人所殺。

translations.literal: Zhenqi was attacked by the barbarians, led his army south; the barbarians pursued and defeated him; Zhenqi fled into the hills and reached Shouyang; Chaoyue and Shibao were killed by others.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians attacked Zhenqi, who led his army south. They pursued and defeated him. Zhenqi fled into the hills and reached Shouyang, but Chaoyue and Shibao were killed.

sentences.zh: 五年，汝陰太守楊文萇又頻破虜於荊亭及戍西。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Administrator of Ruyin Yang Wenchang again repeatedly defeated the barbarians at Jingting and west of the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Yang Wenchang, administrator of Ruyin, again defeated the barbarians repeatedly at Jingting and west of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔進勔號平西將軍、豫州刺史，餘如故，不拜。

translations.literal: An edict advanced Mian's title to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou, the rest unchanged—he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: An edict advanced Mian to General Who Pacifies the West and inspector of Yuzhou, his other posts unchanged, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 其年，徵拜散騎常侍、中領軍。

translations.literal: That year he was summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Palace Secretariat and General of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was summoned to serve as attendant-in-ordinary at the palace secretariat and general of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 勔以世路糾紛，有懷止足，求東陽郡。

translations.literal: Mian, because the world's path was tangled, cherished the wish to know when to stop, and requested Dongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled by the turmoil of the times, Mian wished to know when enough was enough and asked for Dongyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 上以勔啟遍示朝臣，自尚書僕射袁粲以下，莫不稱讚，咸謂宜許。

translations.literal: The emperor showed Mian's memorial throughout to the court officials; from Vice Director of the Secretariat Yuan Can downward, none did not praise it; all said it ought to be granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed Mian's memorial to the whole court. From Vice Director Yuan Can downward, all praised it and said his request should be granted.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「巴陵、建平二王，並有獨往之志。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The two princes of Baling and Jianping both have the will to go their own way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The princes of Baling and Jianping both have the will to withdraw from public life.

sentences.zh: 若世道寧晏，皆當申其所請。

translations.literal: If the world's way becomes peaceful and tranquil, each should have his request granted."
translations.idiomatic: When the times grow peaceful, each of them should have his request granted."

sentences.zh: 」勔經始鍾嶺之南，以為棲息，聚石蓄水，仿佛丘中，朝士愛素者，多往遊之。

translations.literal: " Mian began construction south of Zhongling as his dwelling, gathering stones and storing water, resembling a hill retreat; court gentlemen who loved simplicity often went to visit.
translations.idiomatic: " Mian laid out a retreat south of Zhongling, piling stones and storing water in the manner of a hill hermitage. Court gentlemen who loved simplicity often visited him there.

sentences.zh: 六年，改常侍為侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Attendant-in-Ordinary was changed to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his title of attendant-in-ordinary was changed to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 其年，南兗州刺史齊王出鎮淮陰，以勔為使持節、都督南徐、兗、青、冀、囗五州諸軍事、平北將軍，侍中、中領軍如故，出鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: That year the Prince of Qi, Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, went out to garrison Huaiyin; Mian was made bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs of the five provinces Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and [lacuna in text, likely You], General Who Pacifies the North, Palace Attendant and General of the Palace Guards unchanged, and went out to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Prince of Qi, inspector of Southern Yanzhou, went out to garrison Huaiyin. Mian was made bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You, General Who Pacifies the North, retaining his posts as palace attendant and general of the palace guards, and went out to garrison Guangling.

sentences.zh: 固辭侍中、軍號，許之，以為假平北將軍。

translations.literal: He firmly declined Palace Attendant and the military title; this was granted; he was made Acting General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined the posts of palace attendant and full general. The court agreed and made him Acting General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 七年，解都督、假號、并節。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was relieved of supervision, acting title, and the staff of authority together.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was relieved of his supervisory command, acting rank, and staff of authority.

sentences.zh: 太宗臨崩，顧命以為守尚書右僕射，中領軍如故，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: As Emperor Ming lay dying, he entrusted him as Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, General of the Palace Guards unchanged, and granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Ming entrusted him with the acting post of right vice director of the secretariat, retaining his command of the palace guards, and granted him a full set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，加兵五百人。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, five hundred troops were added to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, five hundred troops were added to his guard.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，月犯右執法，太白犯上將，或勸勔解職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui, the moon transgressed the Right Enforcer of Law and Venus transgressed the Great General; some urged Mian to resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhui era, the moon crossed the Right Enforcer of Law and Venus crossed the Great General. Some urged Mian to resign.

sentences.zh: 勔曰：「吾執心行己，無愧幽明。

translations.literal: Mian said: "In holding my heart and conducting myself, I have no shame before the hidden and the manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Mian said: "In heart and conduct I have nothing to fear before the living or the dead.

sentences.zh: 若才輕任重，災眚必及，天道密微，避豈得免。

translations.literal: If talent is light and burden heavy, calamity must reach one; heaven's way is subtle and hidden—how can avoidance escape it?"
translations.idiomatic: If my talent is slight for my burden, calamity will find me. Heaven's way is subtle—how can fleeing avoid it?"

sentences.zh: 」桂陽王休範為亂，奄至京邑，加勔使持節、領軍，置佐史，鎮扞石頭。

translations.literal: " When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled and suddenly reached the capital district, Mian was given the staff of authority and command of the guards, staff officers appointed, and he garrisoned and defended Stone Citadel.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Prince of Guiyang, Liu Xiufan, rebelled and suddenly reached the capital, Mian was given the staff of authority and command of the palace guards, with a full staff, and garrisoned Stone Citadel.

sentences.zh: 既而賊眾屯朱雀航南，右軍王道隆率宿衛向朱雀，聞賊已至，急信召勔。

translations.literal: Soon after the rebel host encamped south of the Zhuque Floating Bridge; General of the Right Wang Daolong led the palace guard toward Zhuque; hearing the rebels had arrived, he urgently summoned Mian by messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels encamped south of the Zhuque Floating Bridge. General of the Right Wang Daolong led the palace guard toward Zhuque and, hearing the enemy had arrived, urgently summoned Mian.

sentences.zh: 勔至，命閉航，道隆不聽，催勔渡航進戰。

translations.literal: When Mian arrived, he ordered the bridge closed; Daolong would not listen and urged Mian to cross the bridge and advance to battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian arrived he ordered the bridge closed. Daolong refused and pressed Mian to cross and give battle.

sentences.zh: 率所領於航南戰敗，臨陳死之，時年五十七。

translations.literal: Leading his command he was defeated south of the bridge and died in the battle line, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Leading his troops he was defeated south of the bridge and died in the fighting line at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 事平，詔曰：「夫義實天經，忠惟人則，篆素流采，金石宣輝，自非識洞情靈，理感生極，豈有捐軀衛主，捨命匡朝者哉！

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, an edict said: "Righteousness is truly heaven's constant; loyalty is man's rule; seal-script and silk stream with splendor, metal and stone proclaim radiance—unless one penetrates the spirit in feeling and is moved by reason to life's utmost, how could there be those who cast aside their bodies to guard the lord and abandon life to set the court aright!
translations.idiomatic: When the revolt was crushed, an edict said: "Righteousness is heaven's constant and loyalty mankind's rule. They shine in silk and stone. Unless one's spirit is moved to the utmost, who would give his body to guard his sovereign and his life to set the dynasty aright?

sentences.zh: 故持節、鎮軍將軍、守尚書右僕射、中領軍鄱陽縣開國侯勔，思懷亮粹，體業淹明，弘勳樹績，譽洽華野。

translations.literal: The late bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, General of the Palace Guards, and Marquis of Poyang county Liu Mian—his thought and bosom were bright and pure, his person and achievement broad and clear, great merit established, fame filling court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: The late bearer of the staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, acting right vice director of the secretariat, general of the palace guards, and founding marquis of Poyang, Liu Mian, was bright and pure in mind, accomplished in person and office, built great merit, and won fame throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 綢繆顧託，契闊屯夷，方倚謀猷，翌康帝道。

translations.literal: Intimately entrusted in the testament, bound in hardship through turmoil, he was just then relied on for counsel and strategy to assist and bring peace to the imperial way.
translations.idiomatic: Intimately entrusted at the emperor's deathbed, bound to him through hardship and turmoil, he was just then relied on to counsel and secure the imperial way.

sentences.zh: 逆蕃扇禍，逼擾京甸，援桴誓旅，奉律行師。

translations.literal: The rebellious barbarian fanned calamity and pressed upon the capital district; he took up the drum and pledged the host, upholding law in marching the army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel fanned disaster and pressed upon the capital. He took up the drum, pledged his troops, and marched under discipline to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 身與事滅，名隨操遠。

translations.literal: His person perished with the affair; his name follows his conduct into the distance.
translations.idiomatic: His body perished with the cause, but his name follows his conduct into the distance.

sentences.zh: 朕用傷悼，震慟於厥心。

translations.literal: We therefore grieve and mourn, shaken to the depths of Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: We grieve and are shaken to the depths of Our heart.

sentences.zh: 昔王允秉誠，卞壼峻節，均風往德，歸茂先軌。

translations.literal: Of old Wang Yun held sincerity and Bian Hu bore stern integrity; equal in wind with past virtue, he returns to adorn the former track.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Wang Yun held fast to loyalty and Bian Hu to stern integrity. Mian matches their ancient virtue and returns honor to their path.

sentences.zh: 泉途就永，冤逝無追，思崇徽策，式光惇史。

translations.literal: The spring road has reached eternity; wronged departure cannot be pursued; We think to exalt his honored decree and thereby glorify the sincere histories.
translations.idiomatic: The road to the springs is forever; his wrongful death cannot be undone. We would exalt him with honored titles and let his glory shine in the histories.

sentences.zh: 可贈散騎常侍、司空，本官、侯如故，諡曰忠昭公。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Palace Secretariat and Minister of Works, his original offices and marquisate unchanged; his posthumous title shall be Loyal and Illustrious Duke."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously honored as attendant-in-ordinary at the palace secretariat and Minister of Works, his original offices and marquisate unchanged, with the posthumous title Loyal and Illustrious Duke."

sentences.zh: 子悛嗣，順帝升明末，為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Juan succeeded; at the end of the Shengming era under Emperor Shun, he was Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juan succeeded him and, at the end of the Shengming era of Emperor Shun, served as inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 勔弟斅，泰始中，為寧朔將軍、交州刺史，於道遇病卒。

translations.literal: Mian's younger brother Jiao, in the Taishi era, was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Jiaozhou; on the road he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's younger brother Jiao served in the Taishi era as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Jiaozhou but fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 先有都鄉侯爵，諡曰質侯。

translations.literal: He had earlier held the rank of Marquis of the Capital District; his posthumous title was Marquis of Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier held the rank of marquis of the capital district, with the posthumous title Marquis of Integrity.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：吳漢平蜀，城內流血沾踝，而其後無聞於漢；

translations.literal: The historian says: When Wu Han pacified Shu, blood in the city reached the ankles, yet afterward nothing was heard of it in Han;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When Wu Han pacified Shu, blood in the city reached men's ankles, yet afterward Han heard no more of it;

sentences.zh: 陸抗定西陵，步氏禍及嬰孩，而機、雲為戮上國。

translations.literal: when Lu Kang secured Xiling, the Bu clan's calamity reached infants in arms, yet Ji and Yun were executed in the upper state.
translations.idiomatic: when Lu Kang secured Xiling, the Bu clan's punishment reached even infants in arms, yet Lu Ji and Lu Yun were executed in the upper kingdom.

sentences.zh: 劉勔克壽春，士民無遺芻委粒之歎；

translations.literal: When Liu Mian took Shouchun, officers and people had no lingering sigh over scattered fodder and grain;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Mian took Shouchun, officers and people had no cause to lament scattered fodder and grain;

sentences.zh: 莫不扶老攜幼，歌唱而出重圍，美矣！

translations.literal: none did not support the old and lead the young, singing as they came out of the heavy siege—beautiful indeed!
translations.idiomatic: all came out of the siege supporting the old and leading the young, singing as they went—how fine a deed!
